name: Crates
description: Crates is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: USA (Chicago). Developed by Bridge players in Chicago in 1970; spread via Bridge tournaments and summer parties, then nationally.
Time Period: 1970
Historical Development: Enhanced version of Crazy Eights; gained popularity in Chicago, then spread with national Bridge tournaments.
Cultural Significance: Popular at Bridge tournaments and social gatherings.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

rules.objective: Be the first player to achieve the winning condition through strategic play of cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. Setup: prepare players, deck or tiles, and opening layout according to the variant. 2. Turn loop: each player performs one legal action (play, capture, build, bet, or pass/draw as applicable). 3. Resolution: each action updates control of tricks/cards/pot/layout. 4. End condition: when hand-ending criteria are met, scoring is computed and match state advances.
keyRules: Play proceeds in turn order with only legal actions allowed.
Round resolution follows the variant's scoring and bonus conditions.
Match winner is determined by agreed target score or elimination condition.
